title: zestroku doctrine root: owner rules + scope boundary
description:
Root doctrine bead for the zestroku product. Carries the owner rules and the scope boundary every other bead inherits (plan §2/§8):

- Own devices + own LAN only (Express 4K+ .182-class, 50RokuTV .222-class). Never a device the owner does not control.
- Mutations (keypress/launch/install, any settings change) are human-led: one approval per op at point of use. No standing blanket.
- Never commit identifiers (serial/UDN/MAC/ad-id), captures, keys, or firmware images. Fixtures are scrubbed (FIXTURESERIAL-class placeholders).
- Never flash a device. Firmware lane = download + static parse only, offline.
- Documentation-style wording in all instructional text.
- No fuzzing of the shared household LAN in a way that degrades it; cap rates; bench-preferred.
- Shared-tree discipline: Agent Mail reservations before edits; `git commit --only` reserved paths; implementer != verifier (kit-close-needs-evidence).
- Builds/tests via rch (RCH_WORKER=contabo-1 RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1). No darwin workers. CI never needs the network: sim e2e instead.

Acceptance: every other zestroku bead closed with cited evidence; this bead closes last.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: M7c: serve daemon — HTTP API + MCP over one asupersync runtime
description:

WHY: M7 of the comprehensive plan (§9) — the product surface. One `Cx` type across daemon/API/MCP/store is the frankensonos dependency-recipe invariant (§3); polling replaces GENA because ECP has no event surface (ECP-WIRE-DOC §5: empty eventSubURLs).

title: M7d: durable store in zestroku-core (tables + migrations + round-trip proof)
description:
Store bead (plan §5 P5 M7d, §3 schema): the durable store in zestroku-core.

Tables (append-only migration list, frankensonos §7 pattern):
- devices(id TEXT PK, name, ip, model, model_num, firmware, wifi_driver, access_tier, last_seen INT)
- apps(device_id, app_id, name, version, fetched_at INT, PK(device_id, app_id))
- capabilities(device_id, cap, PK(device_id, cap))
- access_tier(device_id TEXT PK, tier, probe_at INT, probe_map TEXT) — open/403/404/untested per command class
- actions(id INTEGER PK, at, client, surface, intent, decision, result, before_state) — M4/M7e consumes this
- diff_results(id INTEGER PK, left_device, right_device, surface, field, left_value, right_value, ran_at)

Backend: fsqlite =0.4.9 async-api (the franken-stack pin, DECIDED Josh 2026-10-10). The round-trip proof validates the AsyncConnection shape on the asupersync runtime. Known hazard (frankensonos §4 item 3): fsqlite engine futures overflow a default thread stack — AsyncConnection-style handle or Box::pin on a dedicated 32MiB thread; never a raw !Send future on a default stack. WAL discipline: short transactions, never hold a txn across network I/O.

- [ ] migrations are an append-only numbered list with a schema_migrations table
- [ ] round-trip test: insert/query/update/delete every table in a real temp-file DB (no mocks)
- [ ] backend decision recorded in the bead comment with the proof output
- [ ] identifiers (serial/UDN/MAC/ad-id) never leave the runtime DB into fixtures

title: M7e: mutation gate — launch/install + per-op confirmation + action log
description:
Mutation gate bead (plan §5 P5 M7e; closes M4): launch/install client paths + per-op human confirmation + action logging.

Scope:
- POST verbs for launch/<app> and install/<app> in zestroku-proto Commands (keypress_raw exists); per-verb pure request builders + response parsers.
- Per-op confirmation gate in zestroku-core: every mutating intent requires --confirm <token> (CLI) or an explicit confirm flag (MCP tool arg); a denied/unconfirmed call returns CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED and logs an actions row with decision=denied.
- Every mutation writes actions(at, client, surface, intent, decision, result, before_state) — before_state = active-app snapshot taken before dispatch.
- Tier gate stays load-bearing: check_tier runs BEFORE the confirmation gate; tier-gate tests extended for POST verbs.

title: M7f: zestroku-sim — virtual devices on loopback (CI-verifiable e2e)
description:

Why mandatory: rch build workers have no speaker LAN; without the sim there is no CI-verifiable e2e path at all. No mocks where a real socket works (AGENTS.md).

title: M8: zestroku doctor — check registry + LAN checks
description:

Check registry in zestroku-core; each check: id, prerequisites, returns pass/warn/fail/skip with detail + evidence + concrete remedy. Prereq-failed checks skip, not fail.

Checks: data dir + store; SSDP responder per device; targets.toml seeds; each device :8060 device-info fetch + latency; tier posture (probe map re-run, §4 map as structured data); store migrations current; suspend-vs-absent discrimination.

Read-only: never mutates device state. Output: table with remedies or --json; exit 0/6/7 pass/warn/fail. Also MCP doctor and GET /doctor.

title: M8: policy.toml — rate limits, allowlists, quiet hours, one choke point
description:
Policy bead (plan §12.5, frankensonos §12.5 adapted — mutation-focused, no media knobs): policy.toml + the choke point.

policy.toml in the data dir: max keypresses/second + launches/minute per client; per-client tool allowlists (keys: client id cli|mcp-stdio|loopback-http); quiet hours during which mutations require explicit confirmation even for cli. Over-limit -> POLICY_DENIED, logged.

Identity: surface + principal (cli / mcp-stdio / loopback-http). Unresolved identity never fails a request; it gets read-only tools. Choke point: every mutating call on every surface goes through one authorize -> snapshot -> execute -> log path in zestroku-core.
